company.introduction: Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust invests in public and private companies selected for their long-term growth potential. Managed by Baillie Gifford, it seeks businesses benefiting from major changes in technology, consumer behaviour and other areas of the economy. Shareholders receive exposure through a listed trust whose share price can trade above or below the value of its portfolio. Returns depend on the underlying companies, valuation changes and expenses rather than sales of a product made by the trust itself. Private holdings require valuation judgements and are less easily traded than listed shares, while the growth-focused approach can produce substantial differences from broad-market performance.

overallConfidence.methodology: Overall confidence combines press sentiment (40%), annual-report tone (35%) and emerging themes (25%). Missing signals are excluded and lower-quality evidence pulls the result towards neutral rather than creating a positive score. Where lexical tone is unavailable, annual-report direction is represented once through emerging themes to prevent double counting.
